text:
Bitcoin surged above the $62,000 threshold on July 3, fueled by a massive $450 million short squeeze following a weaker-than-expected U.S. jobs report. The economy added just 57,000 jobs in June, far below the 110,000 consensus. This cooling labor market triggered a drop in yields and pushed the U.S. Dollar Index (DXY) down to 100.83. The shift in rate expectations broke a 10-day outflow streak for spot Bitcoin ETFs, driving over $220 million in net inflows led by Fidelity's FBTC ($165 million) and Ark & 21Shares' ARKB ($91.84 million).

In traditional markets, the weak payrolls print has strengthened the case for Federal Reserve easing under Chair Kevin Warsh. The retreat of the dollar and yields has lifted the opportunity cost ceiling on non-yielding assets, allowing digital assets to capture institutional capital.
